name: Tsez
confidence_why: Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990 (Kodzasov's instrumental sketch of Kidero Tsez) report no word stress and, on preliminary data, a syllable-tone system, while Khalilov 1999 describes a weak dynamic stress whose place is set by morphological form, and Comrie & Polinsky 2017 and Maddieson, Rajabov & Sonnenschein 1996 state that Tsez prosody has not been studied, so the type of the system remains unsettled.

new_statements.translation: [p. 329] The accentual system is insufficiently studied, therefore tone is not transcribed in the word list. According to preliminary data, Tsez has a system with syllabic tone, typical of the Andic-Tsezic area. Word stress is absent. [p. 9] The dictionary gives no accentological characteristics for the following varieties: Tindi, TSEZ, Hinuq, Bezhta (Kh.), Hunzib, Lak, Tsakhur (G, Ts), Kryz, Budukh, Udi. Word stress is absent in these varieties. [p. 318] In languages with syllabic tone word stress is usually absent ... If a phrasal accent falls on a word, it is placed either on the first syllable of the word or on a 'heavy' non-first syllable (i.e. a closed syllable or one with a long vowel).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Kodzasov's first-hand field sketch of the Kidero variety states that Tsez has no word stress; its accentual system is, on preliminary evidence, one of syllabic (lexical) tone like the rest of the Andic-Tsezic area, but was too little studied to be transcribed. Prominence heard on words is treated as phrasal accent, which in such Daghestanian systems goes to the first syllable or to a heavy (closed / long-vowel) non-initial syllable.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned by Kibrik & Kodzasov. (The secondary ILing RAN 'Малые языки России' page instead claims weak, dynamic, non-fixed stress with main stress on the initial syllable and a secondary stress on the final or penultimate syllable in words of three or more syllables — unsourced, probably after Imnaishvili 1963.)
new_statements.exceptions: None in the source; the authors flag the whole accentual analysis as preliminary ('изучена недостаточно', 'по предварительным данным'). Conflicting descriptions exist: ILing minlang page (weak dynamic initial stress, not fixed); Comrie & Polinsky 2017/2020 only say prosodic contrasts have been noted (citing this very page and NCED p.115) and remain uninvestigated; Maddieson et al. 1996 explicitly defer stress and intonation to future work.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level claim based on elicited isolated nominal word forms (comparative noun dictionary) from Kidero village speakers; phrasal accent placement discussed only generically for Daghestanian (p. 318). Variety: Kidero dialect; Comrie & Polinsky's material is Asakh (Tsebari).
new_statements.first_reading: no word stress according to the source
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement (Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990) describes the speech of the village of Kidero (ЦЕЗ = «цезский, с. Кидеро»), i.e. the Kidero dialect of Tsez proper; Comrie & Polinsky's sketch follows the Tsebari subdialect of Asakh; Maddieson et al. 1996 recorded one speaker (R. Rajabov). All are Tsez proper (dido1241), not the divergent Sagada dialect. No separate glottocode asserted for Kidero.

new_statements.quote: Ударение в Ц. я. динамическое, слабое. Место ударения в слове свободное: в одних словах оно падает на последний слог, в других – на первый. Место ударения зависит от формы слова: 1) В им. падеже в именах ударение в большей части падает на первый слог основы, а в формах косвенных падежей – на последний слог основы: къу́тIи 'договор' – къутIа́ь, ме́сла 'плесень' – месла́. 2) В инфинитиве глагола подударным является суф. -а, а во временах глагола – гласные корня: къикъа́ 'разлагаться' – къи́къых (наст. вр.). В заимствованных словах оно в основном сохраняется на том же слоге, что в языке-источнике. Вопрос о просодических характеристиках Ц. я. изучен слабо.
new_statements.translation: Stress in Tsez is dynamic and weak. The place of stress in the word is free: in some words it falls on the last syllable, in others on the first. The place of stress depends on the form of the word: 1) In the nominative case, in nouns, stress for the most part falls on the first syllable of the stem, while in the oblique-case forms it falls on the last syllable of the stem: qʼúƛi 'agreement' – qʼuƛáʕ, mésla 'mould' – meslá. 2) In the infinitive of the verb the suffix -a is stressed, while in the tense forms of the verb the root vowels are: qʼiqʼá 'to decompose' – qʼíqʼix (present tense). In borrowed words it is mostly kept on the same syllable as in the source language. The question of the prosodic characteristics of Tsez has been poorly studied.

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Tsez has an empty rule; the only existing statement is Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990: 329 'Словесное ударение отсутствует' (there is no word stress; preliminary data point to a syllable-tone system typical of the Andic-Tsezic area), read as 'unclear or contradictory'. Khalilov 1999 differs in type: he asserts that Tsez does have a (weak, dynamic) word stress and gives a morphologically conditioned placement rule with accented examples, and says nothing about tone. So the two Russian sources disagree on whether word stress exists at all; Khalilov does not cite or answer Kibrik & Kodzasov.
new_statements.rule_in_words: A weak dynamic word stress whose position is set by the morphological form rather than by a single fixed syllable: nouns in the nominative are mostly stressed on the first syllable of the stem, oblique-case forms on the last syllable of the stem (i.e. stress shifts toward the case ending); verbs are stressed on the infinitive suffix -a but on the root vowel in tensed forms. Khalilov calls the placement 'free' only in the sense that it is not tied to one syllable (some words final, some initial) and then gives the morphological conditioning. The author himself flags the prosody as poorly studied. Closest list value: morphologically determined (morphologically governed placement, stem/root in the base forms); it is not lexical (unpredictable), since a rule is stated, and not fixed: initial syllable or fixed: final syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: (a) The nominative-initial rule holds only 'в большей части' (for the most part). (b) Loanwords generally keep the stress of the source language (Avar, Russian, Arabic via Avar). (c) The whole account is hedged: 'Вопрос о просодических характеристиках Ц. я. изучен слабо' (the prosody of Tsez is poorly studied).
new_statements.identity_note: Khalilov 1999 describes Tsez as a whole (47 villages of the Tsunta district plus resettled villages; he lists the Asakh, Kidero, Shaitl and Shapikh dialects after Megrelidze, and Tsez proper vs. Sagada after Imnaishvili) and does not tie the stress statement to a dialect. The conflicting Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990 sketch is of the Kidero village variety. No evidence that the disagreement is dialectal.

readall_conflicts: Direct disagreement between the two primary Russian descriptions. Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990: 329 (Kodzasov's instrumental phonetic sketch of the Kidero variety; the catalog's existing statement) say word stress is absent and that preliminary data suggest a syllable-tone system. Khalilov 1999: 322 (Языки мира sketch, no dialect specified) says word stress exists, is weak and dynamic, and is placed by morphological form (nominative nouns mostly stem-initial, oblique cases stem-final; infinitive -a stressed, root vowel stressed in tensed forms), with loanwords keeping source-language stress; he adds that Tsez prosody is poorly studied and does not engage Kibrik & Kodzasov. The other on-disk descriptions do not resolve this: Comrie & Polinsky (2017 ms) §2.4 Prosody p. 5 only note that Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990: 329 and Nikolayev & Starostin 1994: 115 'note the existence of prosodic contrasts in Tsez words' and say 'we have not investigated the area of prosody further. A targeted study is very much needed'; Maddieson, Rajabov & Sonnenschein 1996 list 'the systems of stress and intonation' among topics left for future work. Khalilov's is the only explicit placement rule in print, but it is contradicted on the existence of word stress by an instrumental phonetician, so the language stays unresolved between morphologically governed weak stress and a stressless tone-like system.
